\subsection{The Picard witness \(J=\Pic^0_{C/k}\)}
\label{sec:picardJacobianWitness}

\begin{theorem}[The Picard identity component is a Jacobian witness]
  \label{def:picardJacobianWitness}
  \uses{def:JacobianWitness, def:genus, thm:fga_pic_representability,
    thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety, thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus,
    thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.picardJacobianWitness}
  The identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) carries a Jacobian witness for
  \(C\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
  \uses{lem:curve_geometrically_integral, lem:curve_hypothesis_gap,
    lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus, lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}
  Representability of the relative Picard functor gives \(\Pic_{C/k}\), and its
  identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is a group scheme, smooth, proper and
  geometrically irreducible by \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety}. Those four data
  are the first four fields of the witness; of the four,
  \cref{thm:pic0_smooth} and \cref{thm:pic0_proper} are the ones whose own proofs
  are still open.

  Three further steps are needed, and each is isolated as a lemma because it does
  not follow from the four above.

  First, the hypotheses must be reconciled: \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is constructed for a
  geometrically \emph{integral} curve carrying a \(k\)-rational point, whereas a
  witness is required for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve.
  Geometric integrality is automatic (\cref{lem:curve_geometrically_integral}); the
  rational point is not, and is the single genuine gap
  (\cref{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap}), a gap only over a general base field ---
  over an algebraically closed field it is \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}
  and the witness is \cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed}.

  Second, the smoothness supplied by \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety} carries no
  relative dimension, while the witness records smoothness at the specific
  relative dimension \(g(C)\); the tangent-space identification
  \(T_0\Pic^0_{C/k}\cong H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\) of
  \cref{thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus} supplies the dimension, and
  \cref{lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus} is the resulting refinement.

  Third, the Albanese structure is required for \emph{every} \(P\in C(k)\) and for
  every genus, whereas \cref{thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar} is proved
  over an algebraically closed base field and for \(g(C) > 0\); the extension is
  \cref{lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}. Together these seven data form the
  required witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A smooth geometrically irreducible curve is geometrically integral]
==========
  \(k\)-rational point.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  This assertion is \emph{false} as stated. A smooth proper geometrically
  integral curve need not have a \(k\)-rational point: a conic over \(\mathbb{Q}\)
  with no rational point is a genus-\(0\) example, and there are genus-\(2\)
  curves over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point. Over an algebraically closed
  field a rational point always exists, since a curve there is a nonempty
  Jacobson space whose closed points are rational.

  The lemma is therefore stated here only to name the gap between the hypotheses
  of the witness and those of the Picard construction, and it is not provable in
  this form. Closing it requires either weakening the claim --- carry
  \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a hypothesis of the Jacobian itself, which proves
  something weaker than intended --- or replacing the input by a representability
  statement that needs no section, namely representability of the \'etale
  sheafification (\cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}). That choice is open. The algebraically
  closed case is not affected by it and is \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A curve over an algebraically closed field has a rational point]
  \label{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}
  \leanok
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.hasRationalPoint_of_curve_of_isAlgClosed}
  \uses{def:has_rational_point}
  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically
  closed field \(\bar k\). Then \(C\) has a \(\bar k\)-rational point.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
  \leanok
  Geometric irreducibility over the one-point base \(\Spec \bar k\) makes the
  underlying space of \(C\) irreducible, in particular nonempty, and smoothness makes
  \(C \to \Spec \bar k\) locally of finite type, so that space is a Jacobson space.
  A nonempty Jacobson space has a closed point \(x\). Over an algebraically closed
  field the residue field at a closed point of a scheme locally of finite type is
  \(\bar k\) itself, so \(x\) is the image of a section of \(C \to \Spec \bar k\),
  which is the required rational point.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Which leaf is false and which is merely unproved]
  \label{rem:rational_point_scope}
  \uses{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap, lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}
  \Cref{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap} and \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed} state the
  same conclusion under different hypotheses, and the pair delimits what is open. Over an
  arbitrary base field the statement is false, so it admits no proof and the witness built
  on it rests on an inconsistent hypothesis --- its consequences are vacuously true. Over
  an algebraically closed field the same statement is a theorem. So the open question is
  not the existence of a rational point in general, but which of two formulations is
  claimed over an arbitrary \(k\): representability of \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with
  \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a hypothesis, or representability of the \'etale
  sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), which needs no section
  (\cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}). The remaining obligations of the witness ---
  \cref{thm:pic0_smooth}, \cref{thm:pic0_proper},
  \cref{lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus} and \cref{lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points} ---

\end{remark}

body: "NON-VACUITY IS THE WRONG QUESTION FOR A HYPOTHESIS THAT IS EQUIVALENT TO ITS\
  \ CONCLUSION\n\nDurable lesson from auditing AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.chi_eq_of_bump\
  \ (AJC, LedgerClosure.lean).\n\nThe pattern. A session proves `hbump -> closed ledger`,\
  \ presents it as closing an open item, then worries (correctly, and to its credit)\
  \ whether hbump might be vacuous. Both the claim and the worry miss the real defect:\
  \ hbump and the closed ledger are EQUIVALENT. The converse is three lines\n  rw\
  \ [hledger (D+P), hledger D, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring\nbecause degK is\
  \ an AddMonoidHom and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A -> B` where\
  \ `B -> A` is trivial transports no information; it is a restatement. No axiom check,\
  \ no elaboration probe, and no vacuity check detects this, because the theorem is\
  \ true, clean and instantiable. It is the re-indexing failure mode of I-0399 at\
  \ one level of remove: not `Iff.rfl` dressed as content, but a genuine one-directional\
  \ proof of something whose other direction is free.\n\nThe check to run before claiming\
  \ a hypothesis-elimination is progress: TRY TO PROVE THE CONVERSE. If it takes three\
  \ lines, you reformulated, you did not reduce. Cheap, decisive, and applies to every\
  \ `..._of_bump`-shaped restatement.\n\nSecond lesson, on how to answer a vacuity\
  \ question properly. \"Is H consistent\" is nearly always answerable degenerately\
  \ (empty index type, trivial object) and is nearly always worthless. The informative\
  \ questions are:\n  - is H equivalent to its own conclusion (above);\n  - WHERE\
  \ is H false? Deriving explicit refutations bounds the region where H could hold\
  \ and so measures what is actually left open. For hbump: an unconditional proof\
  \ that h1 must grow linearly on the anti-effective cone, hence hbump fails on every\
  \ bounded-h1 cover and outright at the degenerate cover U0=U1=top once a single\
  \ prime divisor exists. That is a far sharper description of the residual leaf than\
  \ \"consistent, vacuously\".\nA conditional refutation (one taking the thing it\
  \ refutes as a hypothesis, as not_bump_of_notMem_overlap does with hchiAdd) is much\
  \ weaker than an unconditional one; do not read the first as the second.\n\nThird,\
  \ a citation hygiene point that recurred here. Docstrings cited `ResidueField.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric`\
  \ as \"producing a real prime divisor on a curve\". The name does not resolve (no\
  \ such namespace; it is AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.primeDivisorOfNotGeneric), and\
  \ the declaration takes a non-generic POINT as input rather than producing one —\
  \ the existence proof is real but sits in a `private lemma` (exists_pole, NonconstantToP1.lean)\
  \ and is unexported. Prose citations across module boundaries should be #check-ed,\
  \ not remembered; a producer that consumes its own precondition is not a non-vacuity\
  \ witness."

A CLEAN `#print axioms` LINE LIES IN EIGHT DISTINCT WAYS — the workspace catalogue, keyed to `scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`

All eight measured in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, not hypothesised. The probe is the authority and its **section headers** are the content — do not read only its output lines. **Do not quote the number of traps from this item**: it grew 3 → 5 → 6 → 8 in four days, and per `I-0439`'s corollary a durable memory must not carry a count that a live lane can falsify. Read the probe's section headers for the current list.

  (a) **A SORRY-BODIED INSTANCE reached only at a synthesis site.** A theorem that *quantifies over*
      `[HasPicScheme C]` reports clean axioms, because the caller discharges the hypothesis. The
      leak appears one step later, where Lean must synthesize and the only producer is
      sorry-bodied. Measure with a `leakProbe`/`leakControl` pair: identical conclusion and proof
      term, differing only in whether the instance is synthesized. (§8)
  (b) **An UNPROVED named hypothesis in the statement.** Invisible. Most of the cluster-P vanishing
      lane is clean and carries the closed χ-ledger as a hypothesis. (§6b, §6d)
  (c) **A FALSE named hypothesis.** Worse: the theorem is vacuously true and reports clean like any
      other. Happened on the `hrank` leaf, refuted by `O_{P^1_A}/x`. The cure is a non-vacuity
      witness — exhibit an object satisfying the hypotheses and fire the theorem at it. (§6c)
  (d) **An INSTANCE BINDER nothing can instantiate for the ambient object.** The obligation sits in
      square brackets, so it is a hypothesis, so the axiom line is clean and always will be.
      `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` had three such binders, two with no producer for a bare
      `Scheme`; an instance for a more structured cousin (`Over (Spec k)` rather than `Scheme`) is
      WORSE than none, because the grep succeeds. (§6e)
  (e) **An UNROOTED module is not probed at all:** `import AlgebraicJacobian` never reaches it, so no
      `#print axioms` line for its declarations can even be written, and nothing warns.
  (f) **AN INSTANCE DIAMOND**, where two non-definitionally-equal instances can supply the same
      binder, so a file proves correct-looking theorems about a definition pinned to the wrong one.
      This defeats an instantiability check too, because the binders *do* synthesise. The tell is a
      cross-file identity that ought to be `rfl` and is not. Absorbed from `I-0432`; met in the wild
      and now documented at `RiemannRoch/Adelic/ResidueField.lean:786-800` — explicit
      `[Algebra k C.left.functionField]` binders vs the scoped `Scheme.functionFieldAlgebra`, where
      the error message names `chi` rather than the instance. Note `open scoped AlgebraicGeometry`
      alone does not activate it; only `open scoped AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme` does.
  (g) **A REFUTABLE hypothesis** — sharper than (c), because the falsity is *derivable in-tree*: the
      project proves `H → C` and, at every instance anyone would use, `¬H`. The theorem is true,
      axiom-clean, instantiable, consistent, non-vacuous by every probe, and empty. Measured on the
      χ-ledger's `hbump` (probe §2b): iterating it down the anti-effective cone forces `h¹` to grow
      linearly, so it is false on every bounded-`h¹` cover and outright false at `U₀ = U₁ = ⊤` once
      one prime divisor exists. A consistency witness exists (`bump_of_isEmpty_primeDivisor`, on a
      scheme with no prime divisors) and proves nothing. **The only check that finds this**: read the
      PRODUCER's side conditions and ask whether the family the hypothesis quantifies over contains
      a member whose negation the tree proves. Corollary, absorbed from `I-0451`: when a hypothesis
      turns out usable *more generally* than believed, audit the widened quantifier for members
      where the project derives the negation — widening one reading can make it strictly stronger
      exactly where the project can prove the opposite.
  (h) **A HYPOTHESIS EQUIVALENT TO ITS OWN CONCLUSION**, and this is the one to check FIRST because it
      costs a single `rw` attempt. `chi_eq_of_bump` proves `hbump → closed ledger`; the converse is
      three lines (`rw [hledger (pointDivisor P + E), hledger E, degK_add, degK_pointDivisor]; ring`)
      because `degK` is an `AddMonoidHom` and the bump adds exactly one point. A theorem `A → B`
      whose converse is trivial transports no information: it is a restatement, and "is `A`
      satisfiable" *is* "is `B` satisfiable". Absorbed from `I-0456`. **Before believing that
      `H → C` reduces `C` to `H`, try to prove `C → H`.** Two further notes from the same audit:
      "is `H` consistent" is nearly always answerable degenerately and nearly always worthless — the
      informative question is WHERE `H` is false; and a *conditional* refutation (one taking the
      thing it refutes as a hypothesis, as `not_bump_of_notMem_overlap` does with `hchiAdd`) is much
      weaker than an unconditional one, so do not read the first as the second. (probe §2c)

HOW TO CHECK, and it is the only way that works: **ELABORATE A CONSUMER**, do not read the
signature. Write an `example` with only the hypotheses you claim to need, apply the theorem, and
see whether it compiles. Reading binders tells you what is asked for; only elaboration tells you
what can be supplied.

WORKED PAIR, which is why (d) is worth stating rather than just avoiding:
`hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed` and `hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed_curve` have the SAME
axiom line. One is a relocation of the obligation, the other a genuine discharge. Both are
probed side by side in §6d/§6e. The axiom line was never what distinguished them.

CITATION HYGIENE, which recurred in the (h) audit: prose citations across module boundaries should
be `#check`-ed, not remembered. `primeDivisorOfNotGeneric` was cited as "producing a real prime
divisor on a curve"; the cited path does not resolve (it is `AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.…`), and the
declaration *consumes* a non-generic point rather than producing one. A producer that consumes its
own precondition is not a non-vacuity witness.

COROLLARY FOR COUNTING: count probe output by ENTRY, not by LINE. Lean wraps a long axiom list
across several lines, so a per-line filter misclassifies exactly the declarations whose lists are
longest. A published count of "41 clean, 35 leaking of 66" survived a session in this project
without anyone noticing it does not add up.

new modes here as comments rather than as new memory items. Related and deliberately kept separate:
`I-0445` (publish the command, not the count), `I-0439` (prose asserting a gate is still open),
`I-0447` (the positive move — re-read your hypotheses' quantifiers before hunting for machinery).
